style: Say in a relaxed, friendly way, like a kind dad helping with homework.
lines: Every worry is real. Its size is how much help it needs. Drag the card into Small, Medium or Big.
Every worry is real. Its size is about how much help it needs.
Worry shows up in your body. Tap a ring on the kid to see where.
Pick a tool. First, tap the meter to show how worried your body feels.
Pick a tool for your week plan.
Pick a time of day for your practice.
Pick who helps you remember.
Pick the body clue this tool helps.
Tap Next to continue your plan.
Tap Set my goal to start your week.
Tap the meter again. How does your body feel now?
This one is Big. Tell a trusted adult. Keep telling until someone helps.
Breathe in.
Hold.
Breathe out.
Squeeze your fists.
Lift your shoulders.
Curl your toes.
Now let go.
Your meter went down. You reported feeling calmer.
That's okay. Try another tool, or talk to someone.
Your goal is set. Check off each day you do it.
Checked. Nice work.
Your week is done. Tap any reflection chips that fit. Then choose your next week.
Tap Start. Follow the dot around the square. Stay comfortable; never strain.
Tap a Facts, Plan or Brave reply. Say it out loud, or in your head.
Tap Start. Make two tight fists, then let go when the picture changes.
Tap Fold it. Then tap Put it in the box.
Your worry is in the box. Pick a worry time with a grown-up, 10 minutes, not at bedtime, to open it and talk.
You never have to tell the class. Tell one grown-up you trust.
If that grown-up doesn't help, keep telling until someone does.
Danger right now? Call 911.
A spelling test tomorrow.
I can't find my library book.
I have to read out loud in class.
My first swim lesson is tomorrow.
My friend seems mad at me.
We're moving, and I'll go to a new school.
My grown-ups were arguing, and I keep thinking about it.
I got a bad grade, and I'm scared to show my family.
A grown-up asked me to keep a secret, and it feels wrong.
Someone at home is very sick.
Someone online asked me for a photo and said to keep it secret.
An older kid hurts me on the bus and says not to tell.
I've felt worried almost every day for weeks, and it's hard to sleep.
you can't sleep, or it happens before every test.
it's been missing for weeks and you're scared to say so.
you start feeling sick every time it's your turn.
you're scared of the water and no one knows.
it turns into being left out or teased every day.
you feel sad or scared most days for weeks.
anyone gets hurt, or you feel unsafe at home. Then it's Big.
you're afraid someone will hurt you. Then it's Big.
A secret that feels wrong, or that you're told to keep from your family, is always one to tell.
This is too heavy to carry alone. A trusted adult can help you understand it and help you feel better.
Tell a trusted adult right away, even if you already sent something. You won't be in trouble for telling.
Being hurt is never okay. Someone saying 'don't tell' is a sign to tell.
Worry that lasts for weeks, or gets in the way of sleep, school or play, is a sign to get help.
Worry thoughts can loop: what if, what if. They can make it hard to fall asleep.
Your heart beats faster. Your body is getting ready to act, like before a race.
Breathing gets fast and shallow. Fast breathing can make worry feel bigger.
Butterflies, or a stomachache. Lots of kids feel worry in their tummy.
Hands can get sweaty or shaky. Muscles get tight, and tight muscles tell your body it's stressed.
You'll forget every word.
I practiced. I know most of them.
I'll go over the hard ones once more tonight.
One test is one test. I can do hard things.
You'll be in big trouble.
Lots of kids lose a book. Libraries help find them.
I'll check my backpack, then ask the librarian.
I can tell the truth and fix it.
Everyone will laugh.
I can't know what everyone else is thinking.
I'll take a breath and read slowly.
My voice might shake, and I can still do it.
You'll sink.
I can ask my swim teacher for help learning safely.
I'll tell the teacher I'm nervous.
Brave means scared and trying anyway.
They hate you now.
I don't know that yet. Maybe they're having a bad day.
I'll ask, 'Are we okay?'
I can be kind first.
You'll never make a friend.
I made friends before. I can do it again.
I'll say hi to one kid the first day.
New is hard, and I can handle hard.
It's your fault.
Grown-ups argue sometimes. It isn't my job or my fault.
I'll tell a grown-up I trust how it made me feel.
I can take care of me right now.
Everyone will be mad forever.
One grade doesn't decide everything.
I'll show it and ask what to work on.
Telling the truth takes guts, and I have guts.
I need to tell you something important.
Something is worrying me and I need help.
Someone told me to keep a secret, and it doesn't feel right.
Tell a trusted adult if a worry: lasts for weeks, gets in the way of school, home or play, keeps you from sleeping, or is about someone being hurt or not safe.
You started calm. Practicing can help you get ready for a hard day.
You stopped early. Check how you feel. You can try again, or talk to someone.
